sources.entry: Knuff - The debug application for Apple Push Notification Service (APNs).

summary.one_liner: Knuff is a macOS debug app for sending test push notifications through Apple Push Notification Service (APNs).
summary.what_it_does: Knuff lets you send push notifications to APNs with little setup, using a certificate pulled directly from your keychain. You can load and save documents containing a device token and JSON payload, and write custom JSON payloads. It detects whether the Development or Production environment applies and supports universal certificates. It shows error response codes returned by APNs and can export an identity to PEM format (⌘ + E). The README also describes automatic device token retrieval, which requires the separate Knuff-Framework and is not available in sandbox mode. A companion Knuff iOS app is mentioned as being on the App Store.
use_cases: test push notifications during app development
send custom JSON payloads to a device token
export a push certificate identity to PEM
save and reload push test documents
how_to_run: Download the latest version from the releases page linked in the README
notable: No configuration needed to send a test push
Reads the push certificate directly from the macOS keychain
Automatic device token detection via the optional Knuff-Framework
Has a companion iOS app on the App Store
caveats: Requires OS X El Capitan 10.11 or later because of HTTP/2 usage
Automatic token detection needs iOS 8+ and the separate Knuff-Framework, and does not work in sandbox mode
